record.paper_title: Open Problems in Geometric Methods for Instance-Based Learning
record.original_question: How can the storage required for the training set in an instance-based learning system be reduced without degrading the performance of the resulting decision rule?

evidence.quote: How can the storage of the training set be reduced without degrading the performance of the decision rule?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space and let $T=\{(x_1,y_1),\dots,(x_n,y_n)\}\subset X\times\mathcal{Y}$ be a finite labeled training set, where $\mathcal{Y}$ is a finite set of class labels. For a subset $S\subseteq T$, define the associated nearest-neighbor decision rule $h_S:X\to\mathcal{Y}$ by $h_S(x)=y_{i^*}$, where $(x_{i^*},y_{i^*})\in S$ minimizes $d(x,x_{i^*})$ (ties broken by a fixed rule). Given a probability distribution $\mathcal{D}$ on $X\times\mathcal{Y}$ from which $T$ is drawn i.i.d., let the error of a rule $h$ be $\mathrm{err}_\mathcal{D}(h)=\Pr_{(x,y)\sim\mathcal{D}}[h(x)\neq y]$.

Develop a general procedure (and accompanying guarantees) for selecting, given any input $T$, a subset $S\subseteq T$ with $|S|\ll |T|$ such that the resulting decision rule $h_S$ satisfies $\mathrm{err}_\mathcal{D}(h_S)\le \mathrm{err}_\mathcal{D}(h_T)+\varepsilon$ for prescribed $\varepsilon\ge 0$. Characterize the smallest achievable $|S|$ as a function of $T$, of the underlying geometry of $(X,d)$, and of $\varepsilon$, and identify conditions under which storage can be reduced without any degradation of the decision rule's performance.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of reducing training-set storage for nearest-neighbor / instance-based learning (training-set condensation, editing, prototype selection) has been studied extensively since Hart's Condensed Nearest Neighbor rule (1968) and continues to generate active research on coresets and approximation guarantees; no single optimal general-purpose solution is known, and the question as posed remains an open research direction rather than a settled theorem.

status_evidence.title: The Condensed Nearest Neighbor Rule
status_evidence.snippet: Hart's classical algorithm initiated work on reducing nearest-neighbor storage but does not provide optimality or performance-preservation guarantees.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational but partial heuristic approach; problem of optimal reduction remains open.

status_evidence.title: Near-optimal sample compression for nearest neighbors
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work provides approximation guarantees for nearest-neighbor compression but the general optimization is NP-hard and broad open questions remain.
status_evidence.claim: Active research area with partial results; general problem still open.
